task:
Fix the Galaxy map star colours: catalogue spectral classes with a numeric subclass all render as "unknown" (2026-11-01 map review finding M01). apps/web only; no API, SQL or workflow change.

THE BUG (verified on main 7bdf7651):
- Galaxy path: the map API (`apps/api/src/routers/map.py`, viewport/catalogue rows) returns the main star's catalogue `spectral_class` as `main_star_class`, e.g. "G2", "K5", "B5", "M3", "DA6", "N0", "H0", "WC8". `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/galaxy-star-stream.ts` `createCatalogueStarsContribution` forwards it as the primary star `type`, and `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/stellar-presentation.ts` `stellarPresentation()` maps it to a glyph.
- `leadingClass()` uses `/^([OBAFGKMLTY])(?:\s|$|\()/u`, so a joined subclass ("G2", "K5") never matches. The special cases have the same defect after `normalise()` lower-cases the value: `/^h(?:\s|$)/` misses "h0", `/^n(?:\s|$)/` misses "n0", `/^d[abcoqvxz]?(?:\s|$)/` misses "da6"/"dab", `/^w(?:c|n|o)(?:\s|$)/` misses "wc8"/"wn7", the carbon rule misses "c7"/"cn2"/"ms5"/"s4". Result: a live 100-system sample around Sol produced 100 "unknown" descriptors, so every catalogue star draws in the unknown (blue) style.
- The System Map already has a separate numeric-aware helper, `stellarPresentationSubtype()` in `apps/web/src/lib/spatial/system-scene.ts` (strips a trailing subclass and maps N, H, SupermassiveBlackHole, D*, W*, TTS, AeBe, carbon families, then OBAFGKMLTY). The two paths have diverged.

WHAT TO DO:
1. Add ONE shared, pure classifier in `stellar-presentation.ts` (for example `stellarFamilyFromCatalogue(spectralClass, luminosityClass?)` or a normalisation step inside `stellarPresentation`) that accepts every real catalogue form: bare letters ("G", "N", "H", "D"), numeric and decimal subclasses ("G2", "K5", "B5", "M3", "A0", "F8", "L4", "T7", "Y1", "O9.5"), white dwarfs ("D", "DA", "DA6", "DAB", "DB3", "DC", "DQ", "DZ", "DAV", "DX"), neutron "N"/"N0", black hole "H"/"H0", "SupermassiveBlackHole", Wolf-Rayet "W", "WC8", "WN7", "WNC", "WO1", carbon/S-type "C", "C7", "CN", "CJ", "CH", "CHd", "CS", "MS", "S", "S4", "TTS", "AeBe", optional luminosity text ("G2 V", "K0 III", "M1 Ia0", "Ia0"/"I"/"II"/"III"/"IV" giants) and the existing descriptive strings already handled (e.g. "White Dwarf (DA) Star", "G (G2 V) Star", "Black Hole", "Neutron Star"). Case-insensitive; trim whitespace.
2. Use it from BOTH paths: the Galaxy catalogue stars (`stellarPresentation` input from `createCatalogueStarsContribution`) and the System Map (`stellarPresentationSubtype` should delegate to the same family logic so its visible output strings stay exactly as today — existing System Map tests must keep passing unchanged).
3. Return the unknown descriptor ONLY for empty/null input or a genuinely unrecognised value (e.g. "X9", "Q", "?", "Planet"). Do not guess a family from a partial match.
4. Keep the raw catalogue string as the fact: where a hover/label or pick result already shows the star class, it must show the original value (e.g. "G2"), never the derived family label. Do not add new UI in this task.
5. Do NOT change the palette colours, glyph set, materials or `babylon/adapter.ts` beyond what is strictly needed to pass the input through; do NOT make all stars orange or any single colour to hide the bug.

TESTS (vitest, alongside the existing stellar-presentation and galaxy-star-stream tests):
- A table test feeding production-shaped raw values exactly as the map API returns them (single field, no separate subtype) through `stellarPresentation` and asserting the expected glyph for each value listed in step 1, plus the unknown cases in step 3. Include giant luminosity cases ("K0 III" -> warm giant, "B2 Ia" -> the existing hot giant/hypergiant rule as currently defined) only where the current glyph rules already distinguish them.
- An end-to-end pure-function test: a `CatalogueViewportSystem`-shaped fixture with `main_star_class` values ["G2","K5","B5","M3","DA6","N0","H0","WC8","", "X9"] -> `createCatalogueStarsContribution` -> the descriptor the renderer consumes; assert eight distinct non-unknown glyph families for the first eight and unknown for the last two. The point is to prove the API-shaped value reaches a visible family, not just that the palette works.
- Parity test: for every value in the table, the System Map path (`stellarPresentationSubtype` with `bodyType: 'star'`, `spectralClass` set) and the Galaxy path resolve to the same glyph family.
- Existing tests must keep passing; if an existing test asserted the old (wrong) behaviour for a joined subclass, update it to the corrected contract and say so in CHANGES.md.

VALIDATION: in apps/web run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm check`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`. Run the focused spatial tests too. This is a visible rendering change: CHANGES.md must say it needs visual validation (Product E2E/visual lane) before production promotion and that it is not deployed.

CHANGES.md: add a dated 2026-11-01 entry at the top describing the defect, the shared classifier, the forms covered, and the tests. Keep the entry to one short paragraph plus one validation paragraph.
